site.name: Audophone Mine
site.location: Magnolia Mining District / Boulder County, Colorado
overview: Audophone Mine is a documented historic gold-and-silver mine locality in Boulder County's Magnolia-area mining landscape.
Federal mineral records identify Audophone as a past-producing underground gold mine, and USGS topographic mapping preserves a stable named mine location southwest of Boulder.

timeline.text: Audophone was developed as an underground gold mine in Boulder County and is retained in federal mineral-resource records as a past producer.
The Audophone Mine name was preserved on the Eldorado Springs 1:24,000 topographic quadrangle, providing a durable geographic reference for the historic site.

moreHistory: USGS Mineral Resources Data System-derived listings identify Audophone as a Boulder County gold mine developed underground and classified as a past producer; other mapped records also associate silver with the locality.

USGS-derived geographic mapping places the named Audophone Mine at approximately 39.98360, -105.37416 on the Eldorado Springs quadrangle. This is used as a historic mine-level identification point and does not assert the present condition of a shaft, portal, property boundary, or access route.
A focused exact-site media search did not establish a rights-cleared photograph that could be confidently tied to Audophone Mine, so no image is attached.
